title: Follow the Cash: What September and October Revealed About Broadcom's AI Growth
subtitle: Stronger AI sales, additional production capacity and closer financial ties with customers: what’s changed?
summary: September and October's news brings my FY2025 assessment forward: Q3 results, a new Singapore substrate facility, up to US$42 billion in financing for Anthropic and the launch of VMware HyperArmor.
content:
My previous post examined Broadcom's financial position at the end of FY2025. September and October's news brings that assessment forward: stronger AI sales, additional production capacity and closer financial ties with customers. Now, the question is: what’s changed?

September 2026

2nd September: Q3 Earnings and Revenue Guidance

What Happened

Broadcom's results on 2 September showed how quickly the business is expanding. Third-quarter revenue reached US$29.591 billion, up 86% year on year, with AI semiconductor revenue of US$16.7 billion, up 221%. Company-defined free cash flow reached US$13.665 billion (Broadcom Inc., 2026a).

Yet the market's response was subdued. Fourth-quarter revenue guidance of approximately US$34.8 billion fell below the US$35.03 billion analyst consensus cited by Reuters, which reported the shares down more than 1% in extended trading (Rooprai, 2026). For shareholders, strong results alone may not lift AVGO’s share price especially when its outlook falls short of expectations.

Effects on Broadcom

Here we can plainly see that expectations are central to any investment. Continued growth supports higher earnings estimates, but shareholders can still face disappointment if the pace falls short of what the market anticipates. Broadcom also guided to a 66% non-GAAP operating margin, unchanged from a year earlier (Broadcom Inc., 2026a). Revenue expansion should therefore not be treated as an automatic promise of further margin improvement.

29th September: Opening of the Singapore Substrate Facility

What Happened

On 29 September, Advanced Substrate Technologies opened its Singapore facility for advanced chip substrates. TOPPAN's subsequent announcement scheduled operations to begin in December 2026 and described the plant's role in meeting demand for large, complex substrates used in AI and networking equipment (TOPPAN Inc., 2026).

Effects on Broadcom

Timing matters! Simply opening is not enough evidence that a facility is immediately ready to make tangible contributions (such as production or earnings). For Broadcom, this opening can be interpreted as more of a long-term investment supporting future operations: more reliable access to substrates reduces the risk of supply chain disruptions which could delay sales.

October 2026

1st October: Report on Financing for Anthropic

What Happened

On 1 October, Reuters reported that Broadcom had agreed to provide Anthropic with up to US$42 billion in financing, with provision for a financing partner and conversion into Anthropic shares (Wang et al., 2026).

Broadcom's quarterly filing dives even deeper: no customer convertible notes under the US$42 billion arrangement had been issued as of 2 August 2026. It also disclosed a separate lease backstop with maximum potential undiscounted liability of approximately US$29 billion upon full deployment; no payments had been made under that backstop (Broadcom Inc., 2026c, Note 10).

Effects on Broadcom

This effectively puts Broadcom’s own cash on the line for Anthropic, its own customer!

Customer financing is a tricky thing: on one hand, it is a “help you help me” situation wherein Broadcom can support chip sales, but a struggling customer can bring its own problems: fewer future orders and losses on whatever has been loaned to said customer. This has a domino effect: suddenly, cash needed to cover unpaid lease obligations leaves less for dividends, buybacks and debt repayment.

To me, this signals a greater appetite for financial risk as Broadcom pursues further AI growth.

13th October: Launch of VMware HyperArmor

What Happened

Broadcom introduced VMware HyperArmor on 13 October to strengthen security within VMware Cloud Foundation environments (Broadcom Inc., 2026b).

Effects on Broadcom

To me, HyperArmor gives customers another reason to stay with VMware. Better security can encourage renewals and further spending on Cloud Foundation, helping Broadcom earn more from its existing customer base.

What Does This All Mean?

I can confidently say that Broadcom is really ramping up its growth ambitions: expanding capacity, strengthening VMware and helping customers finance purchases. To me, these developments point to a company pursuing bigger opportunities with a greater appetite for financial risk.

This is exactly what I like to see in a growth stock, and as such, I remain positive on its current direction.
